findings.problem: The path option lets in anyone hurt by a friend in any way (a friend who cheated, left, or stole). Athanasius's situation is specific: people who seemed to be friends slander you with idle talk, while enemies taunt you, and it grieves you. The option has no slander in it at all, so it is the only gate and it is wide open.
findings.evidence: [00391] Ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ὀνειδίζωσι θλίβοντες οἱ ἐχθροὶ, καὶ φλυαροῦντες διαβάλλωσιν οἱ δοκοῦντες εἶναι φίλοι, καὶ λυπηθῇς ἐν τῇ ἀδολεσχίᾳ σου πρὸς ὀλίγον... Option in node 'who': "Someone I trusted. A friend."
findings.fix: Option text: "A friend. Or someone I thought was one. They're spreading things about me."

findings.problem: 'reason' drops the first half of his condition, the enemies' taunts (ὀνειδίζωσι θλίβοντες οἱ ἐχθροὶ). 'seen' softens slander (διαβάλλωσιν) to 'talking about you', and adds 'more than you let on', which he did not write. ἀδολεσχία (echoing LXX Ps 54:3, 'grieved in my complaint') is grief you keep turning over, not grief you hide.
findings.evidence: [00391] ὀνειδίζωσι θλίβοντες οἱ ἐχθροὶ ... φλυαροῦντες διαβάλλωσιν οἱ δοκοῦντες εἶναι φίλοι ... λυπηθῇς ἐν τῇ ἀδολεσχίᾳ σου πρὸς ὀλίγον, ἀλλὰ δύνασαι παρακαλεῖσθαι ὑμνῶν καὶ σὺ τὸν Θεὸν
findings.fix: reason: "If your enemies taunt you, and people who seemed to be your friends slander you with idle talk, and for a while it grieves you as you turn it over, you can still take comfort by praising God with the words of Psalm 55." seen: "People you thought were your friends are spreading lies about you, your enemies are piling on, and it keeps going round in your head."

findings.problem: The path option widens his situation from ALL your friends and relatives hating and hounding you, to any people who dislike your beliefs (online critics, co-workers, strangers). Then 'seen' tells that player it is about friends and family, which does not match what they tapped. 'seen' also softens 'hated and hounded' (μισούμενον καὶ διωκόμενον) to 'turned cold', and turns 'for the truth's sake' into 'what you believe', which could mean any opinion.
findings.evidence: [00365] Ὅταν δὲ σαυτὸν διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν μισούμενον καὶ διωκόμενον παρὰ πάντων τῶν τε φίλων καὶ συγγενῶν βλέπῃς ... ἂν τοὺς γνωρίμους ἴδῃς ἀποστρεφομένους σε, πτήξῃς. Option: "People who can't stand what I believe."
findings.fix: Option text: "My own friends and family, because I stand by what's true." seen: "Your friends and family have turned against you because you stand by the truth, and even people you know turn away when they see you."

findings.problem: 'turn' is null, so the result has no line where the psalm turns toward hope. 'names' 144:10 ('frees His servant David from the deadly sword') is itself the rescue line, not the line that names the threat.
findings.evidence: BSB 144:7 "rescue me from the deep waters, from the grasp of foreigners"; 144:10 "to Him who gives victory to kings, who frees His servant David from the deadly sword". The LXX title of Ps 143 adds 'against Goliath'.

findings.problem: His situation is a tyrant enemy who rises against THE PEOPLE and against you, as Goliath defied Israel and David. The option drops the people entirely, so anyone with a big bully boss lands here. It also sits under 'Someone with power over me', but Goliath was an outside enemy, not someone set over David. 'seen' says 'Something', which widens a hostile person into any overwhelming circumstance (illness, debt), and it drops 'tyrant'.
findings.evidence: [00483] Ἐχθρὸς τύραννος ἐπανέστη τῷ λαῷ καί σοι, ὥσπερ Γολιὰθ τῷ Δαβὶδ, μὴ πτήξῃς. Option under node 'power': "They're coming after me, and they're far bigger than I am."
findings.fix: Move the option to node 'doing' as: "Someone far bigger than me has set themselves against my people, and against me." seen: "Someone powerful and overbearing has risen up against the people you belong to, and against you with them." reason: "If a tyrant rises up against God's people and against you, as Goliath did against David, don't cower. Trust God as David did, and say his words in Psalm 144."

findings.problem: His picture is exact: you are hiding, and the one hunting you comes into your very hiding place without knowing you are there. The option ('I feel cornered, with nowhere left to go') lets in any feeling of being trapped. 'seen' changes the pursuer into 'the danger', so a person, which is his condition, becomes any threat. It also drops 'without knowing it'.
findings.evidence: [00386] Ἐὰν δὲ καὶ συνδράμῃ ὁ διώκων, καὶ μὴ γινώσκων εἰσέλθῃ εἰς τὸ σπήλαιον ἐν ᾧ καὶ σὺ κρύπτῃ, μηδ' οὕτως πτήξῃς
findings.fix: Option text: "Closing in. Even the place I went to hide isn't safe from them." seen: "You've been hiding from someone who is after you, and now they've come right into your hiding place without knowing you're there."

findings.problem: His condition has two parts: your own people hound you, AND many have risen up against you. The option has only the first, so a single conflict with one relative lands here. 'seen' adds 'with them', meaning the many are joining your own people, which the Greek does not say, and 'are against you' is weaker than διώκῃ (hounded).
findings.evidence: [00326] Ἂν δὲ διώκῃ παρὰ τῶν ἰδίων, καὶ πολλοὺς ἔχῃς τοὺς ἐπαναστάντας κατὰ σοῦ, λέγε τὸν γʹ ψαλμόν. Option: "My own family, or the people closest to me."
findings.fix: Option text: "My own people. And now lots of others are turning on me too." seen: "Your own people have turned on you, and more and more others are rising up against you."

findings.problem: 'seen' and the option drop 'wicked' (πονηρῷ βασιλεῖ). He wrote for someone slandered to a ruler who is evil and already hostile, as Saul was. 'A person with power over you' lets in anyone misrepresented to a fair boss.
findings.evidence: [00384] Εἰ δὲ καὶ διεβλήθης πονηρῷ βασιλεῖ, καὶ ὁρᾷς τὸν διάβολον κατακαυχώμενον, ἀναχώρει
findings.fix: seen: "Someone has lied about you to a person with power over you who already means you harm, and the liar is gloating over it."

findings.problem: τὸν διάβολον can mean 'the devil' (research.json renders it 'the devil gloat over it') or 'the slanderer' (a pun on διεβλήθης, i.e. Doeg). The draft silently takes the human reading. Both can be defended, but the site should pick one on purpose, and the research file and the draft should agree.

findings.fix: Keep "the slanderer boasting about it" (it fits Ps 52:1, which is addressed to Doeg) and change research.json's situation to match; or, if the devil reading is chosen, reason: "...and you see the devil gloating over it, step away and say Psalm 52."

findings.problem: 'as if you don't count' loses the 'not yet' (μήπω): they scorn you as one who has not YET been anointed, so it is a present lack of standing, not worthlessness. 'reason' also drops that this is why they want to fight you (διὰ τοῦτο πολεμεῖν ἐθέλοντες).
findings.evidence: [00356] καταφρονοῦντες ὡς μήπω σου χρισθέντος, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πολεμεῖν ἐθέλοντες

findings.problem: 'names' 7:1 names pursuers, not the plotting that is his situation (Ahithophel's counsel). 7:14 is the verse that names the scheming.
findings.evidence: [00332] βουλεύωνταί τινες κατὰ σοῦ, ὡς ὁ Ἀχιτόφελ κατὰ τοῦ Δαβὶδ; BSB 7:14 "Behold, the wicked man travails with evil; he conceives trouble and births falsehood."
findings.fix: names: "7:14" (turn 7:10 can stay)

summary:
I checked all eleven outcomes against the Greek in marc-greek2.txt (lines 00326, 00332, 00336, 00338, 00356-57, 00365, 00384-87, 00391, 00483-84). Every pairing is one Athanasius actually made, in the correct English numbering: 3, 7, 11, 13, 27, 31, 52, 54 with 56, 55, 57 with 142, 144. The 'reason' texts are mostly faithful; the one real gap is that P55's leaves out the enemies' taunts.

The main problems are in the gates. P55's option ('A friend') and P31's option ('People who can't stand what I believe') let in far more people than he wrote for. P31's 'seen' then contradicts what the player tapped. P144's option and 'seen' drop the 'against the people' half of the Goliath situation, and P144 has no 'turn' verse, while its 'names' verse is really the rescue line. P57's option and 'seen' turn 'the pursuer walks unknowing into your hiding place' into any feeling of being cornered. P3's option drops the 'many rising up' half, and P52 drops 'wicked'. Minor: the 'devil' or 'slanderer' reading of διάβολον in P52, 'not yet' in P27, and 7:14 as the naming verse for P7.

P54, P11 and P13 are sound. P54's path and its 56 pairing are right. For P11, 'seen' adds 'part of you wants to run', which is loosely drawn from 11:1 but tolerable. P13 is sound on both of its paths.

I checked all 11 outcomes against the Greek (TLG lines [00329]–[00550]). All psalm numbers are right: every LXX numeral maps correctly to English numbering, and every "also" list matches the Greek. P28 is sound. P137 has one serious error: "ἀλλοτρίων λογισμῶν" means thoughts foreign to you (temptations), not "other people's thinking", and the draft drops the repenting and the sin. The rest are smaller problems where the words shown to the player (the "seen" line or the tapped options) widen or blur his condition. P26: "settle it myself" does not match his "do not give the judgment to a man". P62: "out for your life" is dropped, and his command is turned into a description. P39: "decided to change" is wider than keeping watch over yourself. P6: "God is against you" is wider than a threat from the Lord. P42S: "can't say why" is added and clashes with the "life" path. P64: the children's-arrows image comes from his Greek Bible and is not in the BSB verse cited. There are also a few better "turn" verses, especially 62:5, the exact verse his word ὑποτάσσου echoes. No files were edited.

findings.problem: Mistranslation. ἀλλοτρίων λογισμῶν means alien or foreign thoughts: in the Fathers, logismoi are tempting thoughts, and the image is being carried off to a foreign land. It does not mean 'other people's thinking' or 'someone else's way of thinking', which turns a sin of the mind into outside influence. The draft also drops two conditions: μετέγνως (you repented) and ἐφ' οἷς ἁμαρτάνοντα σεαυτὸν κατέλαβες (where you caught yourself sinning). 'The moment you notice, stop' is also not what παῦσαι τοῦ λοιποῦ says (stop from now on).
findings.evidence: [00475] Ἠχμαλωτεύθης ὑπὸ ἀλλοτρίων λογισμῶν, καὶ ᾔσθου σεαυτὸν ἀπαγόμενον, καὶ μετέγνως, παῦσαι τοῦ λοιποῦ, καὶ μείνας ἐφ' οἷς ἁμαρτάνοντα σεαυτὸν κατέλαβες, κάθου, καὶ κλαῦσον καὶ σὺ, ὡς πεποίηκεν ὁ τότε λαὸς, λέγων τὰ ἐν τῷ ρλςʹ. Draft reason: 'carried off by other people's thinking'; option: 'carried off by someone else's way of thinking'.
findings.fix: reason: "If thoughts that are foreign to you have taken you captive, and you have felt yourself being led away and are sorry for it, stop from now on. Stay where you caught yourself going wrong, sit down and weep, as the exiles did by the rivers of Babylon, and say Psalm 137." seen: "Thoughts that aren't really yours carried you somewhere wrong, you've just caught yourself, and you're sorry." Option in node 'self': "My thoughts carried me off somewhere I never meant to go, and I've only just caught myself."

findings.problem: His counsel is not to hand the verdict to a human being and to ask God to judge. The option and 'seen' make the person want to settle it themselves, meaning revenge. The reason then fails to answer the 'seen': someone taking matters into their own hands is not handing the verdict to anyone, so the advice misses them. The reason also drops his description of the enemies (hands full of blood), which widens the case from violent enemies to anyone making trouble. Psalm 26:9 itself has 'men of bloodshed'.
findings.evidence: [00354] Ἐπιμένουσιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ, οὐδὲν ἕτερον ἢ τὰς χεῖρας ἔχοντες αἱμάτων πλήρεις, καὶ ζητοῦντες ἑλκῦσαί σε καὶ ἀπολέσαι, μὴ δῷς ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ κρῖμα (ὕποπτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἀνθρώπινα)· [00355] ἀλλὰ τὸν Θεὸν ἀξιῶν κριτὴν γενέσθαι (μόνος γὰρ αὐτὸς δίκαιος)… Option: 'To settle it myself. To make them answer for it.'
findings.fix: Option in node 'pull': "For someone to finally judge it. To make them answer for it." seen: "They won't stop trying to ruin you, and you want someone to finally rule on who's in the right." reason: "When your enemies keep on, with nothing in their hands but harm, trying to drag you down and ruin you, don't hand the verdict to any human being, because everything human is open to doubt. Ask God to be the judge, for He alone is just, and say Psalms 26, 35 and 43."

findings.problem: Two problems. (1) 'Seen' drops his condition that these people are out for your life (θέλοντας λαβεῖν σου τὴν ψυχὴν) and widens it to anyone who rages. (2) The reason turns his command ὑποτάσσου (submit yourself) into a description ('the more you yield yourself'). There is also no 'turn' verse, but 62:5 is the exact verse his word echoes: LXX 61:6 πλὴν τῷ θεῷ ὑποτάγηθι, ἡ ψυχή μου, which is BSB 'Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him'.
findings.evidence: [00393] πρὸς δὲ τοὺς ὁρμῶντας ἀγρίως κατὰ σοῦ, καὶ θέλοντας λαβεῖν σου τὴν ψυχὴν, ἀντίθες σὺ τὴν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν σου ὑποταγὴν, καὶ θάῤῥει. [00394] Ὅσῳ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι μαίνονται, τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὑποτάσσου σὺ τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ λέγε τὰ ἐν τῷ ξαʹ.
findings.fix: seen: "They're coming at you savagely, out to destroy you, and you've chosen to meet it with stillness and trust." reason: "Against people who come at you savagely and want your life, set your submission to your God, and take heart: the more they rage, the more yield yourself to the Lord. Say Psalm 62." turn: "62:5"

findings.problem: The option 'I decided to change' is much wider than προθέμενος προσέχειν σαυτῷ (having resolved to keep watch over yourself; compare 39:1 'I will watch my ways'). Any change, even a practical one, qualifies. 'It's got harder' does not say what attacks. The 'seen' also drops his last condition, that you want to steel yourself against it (θέλῃς ἐπαλείφειν σαυτὸν κατ' αὐτοῦ).
findings.evidence: [00374] Ἀλλὰ δὴ καὶ σὺ, προθέμενος προσέχειν σαυτῷ, ἐὰν βλέπῃς ἐπιτιθέμενον τὸν ἐχθρὸν (τότε γὰρ μᾶλλον ἐπεγείρεται κατὰ τῶν τοιούτων), καὶ θέλῃς ἐπαλείφειν σαυτὸν κατ' αὐτοῦ, ᾆδε τὸν ληʹ ψαλμόν.
findings.fix: Option in node 'self': "I made up my mind to keep a closer watch on myself, and the temptation has hit harder since." seen: "You resolved to keep watch over yourself, the pull has come at you harder ever since, and you want to stand firm against it."

findings.problem: ἀπειλή is a threat, and the case is sensing a threat from the Lord. The 'seen' ('God is against you') widens this to anyone who feels God is opposed or distant. The reason's 'warning' softens the word. Both psalms open on rebuke in anger (6:1, 38:1), so 'rebuking' stays inside his case.
findings.evidence: [00329] Αἰσθόμενος δὲ ἀπειλῆς τοῦ Κυρίου, ἐὰν διὰ τοῦτο ταραττόμενον σεαυτὸν βλέπῃς, δύνασαι λέγειν τὸν ϛʹ καὶ τὸν λζʹ.
findings.fix: seen: "It feels as if God is rebuking you, and it's shaking you." reason: "If you sense a threat from the Lord hanging over you, and see that it has shaken you, you can say Psalms 6 and 38."

findings.problem: 'Seen' adds 'you can't quite say why'. Athanasius names only sadness (τὸ λυποῦν), and in Psalm 42 the speaker knows why. The addition also contradicts one of the two paths into this outcome: someone who tapped 'Life. It's all just too much' and then 'Making me sad, and I can't shake it' does know why. Separately, 'lightens' understates θεραπεύεται (is healed or tended).
findings.evidence: [00545] τὸ δὲ λυποῦν θεραπεύεται, ψαλλόντων ἡμῶν· [00546] Ἵνα τί περίλυπος εἶ, ἡ ψυχή μου, καὶ ἵνα τί συνταράσσεις με;
findings.fix: seen: "You're sad, and you can't shake it." reason: "Athanasius wrote that when we sing the Psalms, the sadness in us is healed, and the line he gave for it is this one: 'Why are you downcast, O my soul?'"

findings.problem: The children's-arrows image comes from Athanasius's Greek Bible (LXX 63:8 βέλος νηπίων ἐγενήθησαν αἱ πληγαὶ αὐτῶν). The BSB turn verse, 64:7, says 'But God will shoot them with arrows', so a player looking for his image in their Bible will not find it. The paraphrase also cuts the genitive absolute ψάλλοντός σου: their blows become children's arrows as you sing. Singing is his means, not a separate instruction.
findings.evidence: [00396] Ἐκφοβούντων δὲ τῶν ἐχθρῶν καὶ μὴ παυομένων τοῦ ἐνεδρεύειν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξερευνώντων πᾶν κατὰ σοῦ, κἂν πλῆθος ὦσι, μὴ ὑπενδῷς· [00397] βέλη γὰρ νηπίων ἔσονται τούτων αἱ πληγαὶ, ψάλλοντός σου τὸν ξγʹ, καὶ τὸν ξδʹ, καὶ ξθʹ, καὶ οʹ. BSB 64:7: 'But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded.'
findings.fix: reason: "When your enemies keep trying to frighten you, lying in wait and searching out everything against you, however many they are, don't give in: as you sing Psalms 64, 65, 70 and 71, their blows will be no more than children's arrows (his Greek Bible reads 64:7 that way)."

findings.problem: His case is not only knowing you sinned. It is being ashamed, repenting and asking for mercy. The option on the path ('I did something wrong, and I know it') lets in someone who knows but is not sorry. The 'seen' check partly catches this with 'want to come back'.
findings.evidence: [00383] Ἀλλ' ἥμαρτες, καὶ ἐντραπεὶς μεταγινώσκεις καὶ ἐλεηθῆναι ἀξιοῖς, ἔχεις τοὺς τῆς ἐξομολογήσεως καὶ μετανοίας λόγους ἐν τῷ νʹ.
findings.fix: Option in node 'self': "I did something wrong. I know it, I'm ashamed, and I want to be forgiven." seen: "You've done wrong, you're ashamed of it, and you want to be forgiven."

findings.problem: Athanasius's quotation reads 'The Lord is my helper' (Κύριος ἐμοὶ βοηθός). In the BSB the word 'helper' is in 118:7, not 118:6. The current turn, 118:5, comes before the naming verse. 118:7 carries his exact word and is itself the turn.
findings.evidence: [00549] τὸ δὲ φοβηθὲν ἐπιῤῥώσει τῇ ἐλπίδι ἐν τῷ λέγειν· [00550] Κύριος ἐμοὶ βοηθὸς, καὶ οὐ φοβηθήσομαι τί ποιήσει μοι ἄνθρωπος. BSB 118:7: 'The LORD is on my side; He is my helper.'

findings.problem: Athanasius's own word ἀκηδιάσῃς (grow weary) comes from this psalm's LXX title, which the BSB renders 'A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint'. The superscription names his situation more exactly than 102:4.
findings.evidence: [00462] … ἐὰν διὰ τὰς συνοχὰς τοῦ βίου ὡς πτωχὸς γενόμενος ἀκηδιάσῃς ποτὲ, καὶ θέλῃς παρακληθῆναι, ἔχεις τὸν ραʹ ψαλμόν. BSB superscription: 'A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before the LORD.'
findings.fix: If the result format can show a superscription, set names to the Psalm 102 superscription; otherwise keep 102:4.

findings.problem: The names verse (42:5) and the turn verse (42:11) are the same refrain, word for word up to the final clause, so the result would show nearly the same line twice.
findings.evidence: BSB 42:5 and 42:11 both read 'Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him…'
findings.fix: turn: "42:8" ('The LORD decrees His loving devotion by day, and at night His song is with me'), or keep 42:5 alone and let its second half serve as the turn.

findings.problem: The "seen" line and the option text misread the Greek. Athanasius has someone fall among enemies, escape them by wits and slip out of the plot they laid against him (David feigning madness before Abimelech, per the superscription). The draft turns it into someone who was asked to join a plan and said no, which is peer pressure and a different situation. "Fell in with" also means "started keeping company with", which is wrong. The reason says "sing ... with them", but ἐπ' αὐτῶν means in their presence.
findings.evidence: [00368] Ἐμπεσὼν δὲ εἰς τοὺς ἐχθροὺς, καὶ σοφῶς αὐτοὺς διαφυγὼν, καὶ ἐκκλίνας ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῶν, εἰ θέλεις εὐχαριστῆσαι, συγκαλέσας τοὺς πραεῖς ἄνδρας, ἐπ' αὐτῶν ψάλλε τὸν λγʹ. The draft has seen "you got out by wisely refusing their plan" and option (out) "I got out by refusing to go along with something." In the Greek, ἐπιβουλή is a plot against someone and ἐκκλίνας means turning aside from it. BSB superscription: "when he pretended to be insane before Abimelech, so that the king drove him away."
findings.fix: seen: "You fell into the hands of people who meant you harm, and you got away by keeping your wits about you." Option in "out": "People who meant me harm had me cornered, and I thought my way out." reason: "When you have fallen among enemies but wisely got away and slipped out of their plot, and you want to give thanks, call gentle people together and sing Psalm 34 in front of them." Optionally set names to "34:4" ("I sought the LORD, and He answered me; He delivered me from all my fears"), which names the rescue. 34:3 names the gathering.

findings.problem: The draft drops οὕτως ("thus afflicted"). The sentence follows straight on from the Psalm 3 case, being hunted by your own people with many rising against you, and "thus" ties the thanksgiving to that trouble. The reason, the seen line and the option all widen it to any distress. The option also never says who helped, so help from anyone lands on this result. Separately, LXX 114 is only Eng 116:1-9 (research.json says so). Verses 10-19 are LXX 115, which Athanasius assigns elsewhere (§24, to faith).
findings.evidence: [00326] Ἂν δὲ διώκῃ παρὰ τῶν ἰδίων, καὶ πολλοὺς ἔχῃς τοὺς ἐπαναστάντας κατὰ σοῦ, λέγε τὸν γʹ ψαλμόν. [00327] Εἰ δὲ οὕτως θλιβόμενος ἐπεκαλέσω τὸν Κύριον, καὶ εἰσακουσθεὶς θέλεις εὐχαριστεῖν, ψάλλε τὸν τέταρτον, καὶ οδʹ, καὶ ριδʹ. The draft's option is "I cried out for help, and help came." Its also field is [75, 116].
findings.fix: reason: "When you have been hounded like that, by your own people, with many rising against you, and you called on the Lord and He heard you, and now you want to give thanks, sing Psalms 4, 75 and 116 (verses 1-9)." seen: "People close to you turned against you. You called out to God, He heard you, and now you want to say thank you." Option in "out": "People close to me turned on me. I cried out to God, and He answered." Record also as 75 and "116:1-9", not the whole of 116.

findings.problem: This is a stretched pairing. Athanasius's situation is wanting to embolden yourself and others toward godliness, by showing that hope in God does not shame and makes the soul fearless. He did not write it for someone gripped by a vague, nameless dread. The "seen" line and the path (life -> "Making me afraid" -> "Of everything, and nothing in particular") put this result in front of an anxious person he never addressed, and drop the "yourself and others" and the toward-godliness aim. names 91:5 is the result (the fearless soul), not the situation.
findings.evidence: [00425] Παραθαρσῦναι θέλων σεαυτὸν καὶ τοὺς ἑτέρους εἰς θεοσέβειαν, καὶ ὡς εἰς τὸν Θεὸν ἐλπὶς οὔτε καταισχύνει, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄφοβον τὴν ψυχὴν κατασκευάζει, αἴνει τὸν Θεὸν, λέγων τὰ ἐν τῷ ϙʹ. The draft's seen is "You're afraid, and you can't even say of what."
findings.fix: seen: "Fear keeps creeping in, and you want to take heart in God again, and help the people around you take heart too." Option in "fear": "I'm afraid, and I want to find my courage in God again, for me and for the people around me." names: "91:2" ("You are my refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust"). It's shaking me." reason (optional, to keep καταθυμίως ζῶντας): "When you see the ungodly living in peace and plenty, just as they please, while the righteous suffer, say Psalm 73, so that you are not scandalised or shaken."

findings.problem: This is a path problem. P41 is reached only through source -> "Someone I love is going through it." Athanasius's person is looking at many poor and needy people, not at a loved one, so the person he wrote for would not tap that option, and anyone who does is then offered a situation that does not follow from it. Also, ἀποδέχεσθαι means to welcome or commend, which is warmer than "honour".

findings.problem: The "seen" line and the option make the player half-agree with the mockers ("part of you is tempted to join them" / "part of me wants to agree"). Athanasius's situation is hearing people blaspheme against Providence, and his command is not to share their impiety but to intercede. The warning does not presuppose inner agreement. As written, the result is aimed at a doubter more than at the hearer he addressed. It is defensible, since the command implies the risk exists, but it goes one step past his words.
findings.evidence: [00339] Ἐπειδὰν βλασφημούντων τινῶν κατὰ τῆς Προνοίας ἀκούσῃς, μὴ κοινώνει μὲν αὐτῶν τῇ ἀσεβείᾳ, ἐντυγχάνων δὲ τῷ Θεῷ, λέγε τὸν ιγʹ καὶ νβʹ.

Option in "world": "People around me sneer at the idea that God is looking after anything, and it's getting to me." reason: say "don't share in their ungodliness" instead of "don't join in their contempt".

summary: I read each Greek sentence in marc-greek2.txt and checked it against tree.json and the BSB. P12, P20 and P46 are sound; P18 is paired correctly (Migne ιζ' = Eng 18 over the TLG's ις) but its option needs a fix. Three must-fixes. P34 misreads ἐκκλίνας ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπιβουλῆς: escaping a plot laid against you becomes \"refusing their plan\", which reads as peer pressure. P4 drops οὕτως, which ties the thanksgiving to the Psalm 3 trouble (hounded by your own people), and 116 should be only verses 1-9 (LXX 114). P91 is a stretch: Athanasius wrote it for someone wanting to embolden themselves and others toward godliness, not for a vague, nameless fear. Should-fixes: the P18 option makes the rescue self-made and blurs it with P34. The P37 seen drops the oppression of the little ones and the wish to warn others (and 37:2 should be its turn). The P73 option says \"cheat and lie\" where the Greek has ἀσεβεῖς (the ungodly). P41 can only be reached through \"Someone I love is going through it\", which the person Athanasius described would not tap. One consider: P14's \"part of me wants to agree\" adds inner agreement to a situation about hearing blasphemy.

findings.problem: The option on the path turns Athanasius's situation into someone else's. He wrote for a person who longs hard for God while enemies taunt him; the remedy is hope, not an argument. The option leaves out the longing, softens the taunt into an honest question, and adds a need for an answer ('I don't know what to say'). That is a person looking for apologetics. It also sits under 'Nothing's wrong, exactly', yet his person is under scorn and 42:3 has tears for food. 'seen' and 'reason' also soften 'enemies' to 'people', and 'taunting' to 'asking' in 'seen'.
findings.evidence: Sect. 19 [00377-78]: 'Εἶτα ἐὰν, πάνυ τὸν πόθον ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεὸν, ἀκούσῃς τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὀνειδιζόντων, μὴ ταράσσου· ἀλλὰ συνιεὶς τὸν ἐκ τοῦ τοιούτου πόθου ἀθάνατον καρπὸν, παρακάλει σαυτοῦ τὴν ψυχὴν τῇ εἰς Θεὸν ἐλπίδι ... λέγε τὸν μαʹ'. Option: 'An answer. People ask me where God is in all this, and I don't know what to say.' Seen: 'people keep asking you where He is.' Reason: 'hear people taunting you'.
findings.fix: Option (keep it under 'missing', and see the P84 fix so the two do not collide): 'Him. I ache for God, and people mock me for it.' Seen: 'You long for God with everything in you, and people mock you for it: "Where is your God?"' Reason: 'If you long for God with all your heart and hear your enemies taunting you, don't be troubled. Knowing the undying fruit of that longing, comfort your soul with hope in God, and ease its griefs in this life, with Psalm 42.' Names: consider 42:10 ('my enemies taunt me ... "Where is your God?"'), which matches ἐχθρῶν ὀνειδιζόντων exactly. Keep turn 42:5.

findings.problem: The option widens his situation to any hardship that has ended. Athanasius wrote for the end of God's anger and release from captivity. Psalm 85 is about forgiven sin and withdrawn wrath (85:2-3), so a person whose illness or work crisis has just ended would be told, in effect, that it was God's fury. 'seen' says 'The anger is over' without saying whose, and a player will read it as their own anger. The context shows it is God's: the nearby pairing for LXX 73 reads 'ὅταν μὲν ὀργισθῇ ὁ Θεὸς ἐπὶ τὸν λαὸν', and 85:3 says 'You turned from Your burning anger'.
findings.evidence: Sect. 22 [00421]: 'Παυσαμένης δέ ποτε τῆς ὀργῆς, καὶ τῆς αἰχμαλωσίας λυθείσης, ἐὰν θέλῃς εὐχαριστῆσαι, ἔχεις εἰς τὸ λέγειν τὰ ἐν τῷ πδʹ καὶ ρκεʹ.' Option: 'The storm is over. It's finally quiet.' Seen: 'The anger is over and you're free again'.
findings.fix: Option: 'It felt like God was against me. Now that's over, and I'm free.' Seen: 'God's anger has passed, you've been set free, and you want to thank Him.' Reason is faithful; optionally make it 'When His anger has passed at last and the captivity is over...'. Psalms 85 and 126 (πδʹ, ρκεʹ = LXX 84, 125) are correct. Names 85:1 and turn 85:8 are right.

findings.problem: His condition is persecution: someone hunted who flees into the wilderness. 'seen' and the option drop the persecution ('pushed out' also covers being laid off or dropped by friends). They also frame the need as 'People' and put it under 'Nothing's wrong, exactly. But something's missing.' Being hunted into the desert is not 'nothing's wrong', and what Athanasius counters is the fear of being alone, not a lack of company.
findings.evidence: Sect. 20 [00395]: 'Καὶ ἐὰν μὲν διωκόμενος εἰς ἐρημίαν ἀπέλθῃς, μὴ φοβηθῇς ὡς μόνος ὢν ἐκεῖ, ἔχων δὲ τὸν Θεὸν ἐκεῖ καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὀρθρίζων ψάλλε τὸν ξβʹ.' Path: 'Nothing's wrong, exactly. But something's missing.' then 'People. I've been pushed out, and I'm on my own now.'
findings.fix: Move the option to the 'In the middle of something hard' branch, worded: 'People turned on me and drove me out. Now I'm alone, far from everyone.' Seen: 'People set against you have driven you out, and now you're somewhere lonely, afraid you're on your own.' The reason is faithful; keep it. Names 63:1 is fine; the superscription ('when he was in the Wilderness of Judah') is the closest line to his situation if the renderer can show it.

findings.problem: His object of longing is God's house and His eternal dwelling places, as Paul longed to depart and be at home with the Lord. The option ('I long to be near Him') is longing for God Himself, which is Athanasius's wording for Psalm 42 (πόθον εἰς τὸν Θεόν). The two results cannot be told apart, and 'seen' ('where God is') is wider than his object.
findings.evidence: Sect. 22 [00420]: 'Καὶ ἐὰν, βλέπων τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τὰ αἰώνια αὐτοῦ σκηνώματα, τὸν πόθον ἔχῃς εἰς αὐτὰ, ὡς εἶχεν ὁ Ἀπόστολος, λέγε καὶ σὺ τὸν πγʹ ψαλμόν.' Option: 'Him. I long to be near Him.' Seen: 'You long to be where God is.'
findings.fix: Option: 'Home. I long for His house, the place where He lives, for good.' Seen: 'You long for God's house, and for the home with Him that lasts forever.' The reason is faithful; keep it. Names 84:2 is right.

findings.problem: The option narrows πειρασμούς (trials and temptations) to a temptation to sin, and it adds a condition he never set: 'without giving in'. His condition is that the person takes the trials as a proving and wants to give thanks once they are past. The reason also turns his condition into a general statement ('Temptations are how we are tested') and adds 'safely'.
findings.evidence: Sect. 25 [00478]: 'Τοὺς δὲ πειρασμοὺς ἡγούμενος εἶναί σου δοκιμὴν, μετὰ τοὺς πειρασμοὺς ἐὰν εὐχαριστῆσαι θελήσῃς, ἔχεις τὸν ρληʹ ψαλμόν.' Option: 'I came through a temptation without giving in.' Reason: 'Temptations are how we are tested. When you want to thank God once a test is safely past...'
findings.fix: Option: 'I was put to the test, and I can see now it was proving me. It's over.' Reason: 'If you take your trials as a testing of you, and want to give thanks once they are over, you have Psalm 139.' Seen is fine. Names 139:23 ('test me') is right.

findings.problem: He joins three objects of wonder: the order of creation, the grace of Providence in it, and the holy commands of the law. 'seen' drops the law, and the option drops both Providence and the law. The option also swaps order (τάξις) for beauty ('how beautifully everything is made'). Half of Psalm 19 (vv. 7-11) is about the law, and a nature-lover who taps 'beautiful' is not quite his person.
findings.evidence: Sect. 17 [00350]: 'Θαυμάζεις τὴν τῆς κτίσεως τάξιν, καὶ τὴν εἰς αὐτὴν τῆς Προνοίας χάριν, τοῦ τε νόμου τὰ ἱερὰ προστάγματα, ψάλλε τὸν ιηʹ καὶ τὸν κγʹ.' Option: 'I keep noticing how beautifully everything is made.' Seen: 'You're marvelling at how the world is ordered, and at God's care in it.'
findings.fix: Option: 'Everything seems in its right place: the world around me, and what God asks of me.' Seen: 'You're marvelling at how well the world is ordered, at God's care in it, and at how good His commands are.' The reason is faithful, and 19 and 24 are correct.

findings.problem: 'I was corrected' does not say by whom, so a person corrected by a boss or a parent who was lenient would land on a result about the Lord's judgment. His condition is having learned the Lord's power to judge, and that He mixes mercy into His judgment, and wanting to draw near to Him.
findings.evidence: Sect. 23 [00461]: 'Καὶ ἐὰν, μαθὼν αὐτοῦ τὴν κριτικὴν δύναμιν, καὶ ὅτι ἐλέῳ τὴν κρίσιν κεράσας κρίνει ὁ Κύριος, θελήσῃς αὐτῷ προσελθεῖν, ἔχεις εἰς τοῦτο λόγους τοὺς ἐν τῷ ρʹ.' Option: 'I was corrected, and I found mercy in it.'
findings.fix: Option: 'God set me straight, and He was merciful in it. I want to be close to Him.' Seen and reason are faithful. Names 101:1 ('loving devotion and justice') is right.

findings.problem: The reason adds a one-psalm-per-step mapping that the Greek does not make: he says to say the fifteen songs at each advance. 'going forward' also loses 'ascending in your deeds', which is growth in how you live. 'names' points to 121:1, outside the headline psalm (120). Psalm 120's own lines ('In my distress', 'Woe to me that I dwell in Meshech') do not name a person who is in a good place and climbing, and he named the fifteen as a set, not any one of them.
findings.evidence: Sect. 24 [00472-74]: 'Ἀλλὰ ἀναβαίνοντα σαυτὸν αἴσθῃ ταῖς πράξεσιν, ὥστε λέγειν· Τὰ μὲν ὀπίσω ἐπιλανθάνομαι, τοῖς δὲ ἔμπροσθεν ἐπεκτείνομαι; ἔχεις καθ' ἑκάστην προκοπὴν εἰς τὸ λέγειν τὰς ιεʹ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν ᾠδάς.' Reason: 'When you sense yourself going forward ... one for each step.' Names '121:1' with psalm 120.
findings.fix: Reason: 'When you sense yourself climbing higher in how you live, so that you can say with Paul, "forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead", you have the fifteen Songs of Ascents to say at every step forward.' Present the result as 'The Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120-134)' and use the shared superscription 'A song of ascents' as the naming line. If one psalm must headline, set psalm to 121 so that names 121:1 falls inside it.

findings.problem: The reason drops his condition ('if you want to bless God for these things'), drops 'and to all' from the goodness remembered, and leaves the participle dangling. The option narrows 'all' (πάντας) to 'everyone around me'.
findings.evidence: Sect. 25 [00485]: 'Εἶτα θαυμάζων τὰς εἰς πάντας τοῦ Θεοῦ εὐεργεσίας, καὶ μνημονεύων τῆς τε εἰς σὲ καὶ εἰς πάντας γενομένης ἀγαθότητος αὐτοῦ, ἐὰν θέλῃς διὰ ταῦτα εὐλογεῖν τὸν Θεὸν, λέγε τὰ τοῦ Δαβὶδ ῥήματα, ἅπερ καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν ἐν τῷ ρμδʹ ψαλμῷ.' Reason: 'Marvelling at God's kindness to everyone, and remembering His goodness to you, bless Him...'
findings.fix: Reason: 'When you marvel at God's kindness to everyone, remember His goodness to you and to all, and want to bless Him for it, say the very words David said in Psalm 145.' Option: 'His kindness, to me and to everyone.' Names 145:9 is exactly right.

findings.problem: 'In and through everything' is his reason (it is fitting to give thanks in all things), not the situation. The situation is wanting to bless God and stirring up your own soul to do it, which is the 'O my soul' of 103:1. The option's 'for everything' also shifts 'in everything' (in every circumstance) to 'for every good thing'.
findings.evidence: Sect. 24 [00463]: 'Καὶ ἐπειδὴ πρέπει διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν εὐχαριστεῖν ἡμᾶς τῷ Θεῷ, ὅτε θέλεις εὐλογεῖν αὐτὸν, ἔχεις εἰς τοῦτο προτρέπεσθαι σαυτοῦ τὴν ψυχὴν, καὶ λέγειν τὸν ρβʹ καὶ ργʹ.' Seen: 'You want to thank God, in and through everything.' Option: 'I just want to thank Him for everything.'
findings.fix: Seen: 'You want to bless God, and to stir your own soul up to do it.' Option: 'I just want to thank Him, whatever comes.' The reason is faithful, and 103 and 104 are correct. Consider names 103:1 ('Bless the LORD, O my soul; all that is within me'), which shows the stirring of one's own soul.

All psalm numbers, including the "also" and "set" lists, convert correctly from the Greek (Septuagint) numbering to English, and every "reason" keeps his meaning apart from the few slips listed. - **Should-fix:**

  - **P84:** the option longs for God Himself, which is Psalm 42's situation. His object is God's house and eternal dwelling places.
  - **P139:** the option narrows trials to temptation and adds "without giving in".
  - **P19:** the option and "seen" drop the law, and the option drops God's care.
  - **P101:** "corrected" does not say by whom, so correction by a person also fits.
  - **P120:** the reason adds "one for each step", and the verse naming his situation comes from Psalm 121, not Psalm 120, which leads the result.
- **Consider:** small drops in P145 and P103.

I walked the draft tree as the four people. Two of them end up misread. The main problems are in the routing, not in Athanasius's pairings.

1. Nurse. Path: where → "In the middle of something hard" → "Life. It's all just too much" → "Wearing me down. I'm running on empty" → P102. This is a good match. His Greek word is ἀκηδιάσῃς, which means listless, with no heart left for anything, and that is her numbness exactly. The "reason" line ("Our nature is weak…") has no blame in it and will speak to her. Two weaknesses. The "seen" line says "poor and empty" and leaves out the listlessness, which is the thing that would make her feel seen. And many numb people would honestly tap "Nothing's wrong, exactly. But something's missing". That branch has no route to 102, so she ends at "I just feel low" → P42S, "You're sad", and numb is not sad. Psalm 102 mostly meets her (102:4 "I even forget to eat my bread", 102:7 "I lie awake"). But 102:10 ("because of Your indignation and wrath… You have picked me up and cast me aside") could read to a burnt-out believer as God being angry with her.

2. The man after the affair. Path: middle → "Me. Something I did" → "I did something wrong, and I know it" → P51. The pairing is exact, and the superscription ("after his adultery with Bathsheba") is his own story, so he will feel seen. The "seen" line leaves out "ashamed" (ἐντραπεὶς), and shame is the centre of his state. That word is in the "reason" line but not in the line shown to him. 51:4 ("Against You, You only, have I sinned") could read as if his wife's injury does not count, and nothing tells him otherwise. Athanasius's advice itself (repentance, mercy) speaks to him.

3. The 16-year-old mocked for his faith. Path: middle → "Someone is against me" → "People who can't stand what I believe" → P31. He is misread. The "seen" line tells him "Friends and family have turned cold because of what you believe". His family has not, and his parents don't even know. The option is broad, but the pairing is narrow: Athanasius says "all your friends and relatives". The natural first tap sends him to the wrong result. Psalm 31 would also frighten more than help him: 31:13 "plot to take my life", 31:10 "my iniquity has drained my strength", 31:17 "let them lie silent in Sheol". Honest homes exist. P42 is Athanasius's case of enemies taunting someone who longs for God, and the psalm's own words are "Where is your God?". P27 is enemies massing and scorning you, and it is reachable only by avoiding the obvious option. Neither is offered where he would look. P42 sits under "Nothing's wrong, exactly", with a condition added that Athanasius never gave ("I don't know what to say").

4. The widow. No option is honest for her. The tree has no route for loss. She would reluctantly tap "Life. It's all just too much" → "Making me sad" → P42S. There the "seen" line says "You're sad, and you can't quite say why", and that would sting: she knows exactly why. Her other likely paths are also misreads. "Missing → People… on my own now" → P63 tells her she was "pushed out". "Someone I love is going through it" → P20 tells her to "stand beside them", and her husband is dead. Psalm 42 itself would meet her well (42:3 tears day and night, 42:4 remembering how things were, 42:5 "Put your hope in God"). His section-28 remedy is for what grieves you (τὸ λυποῦν), which covers her honestly, as long as no one claims he spoke of death.

The findings below fix all of this using only pairings in research.json recon.entries. No new pairings are proposed. Nothing was edited.

findings.problem: The obvious answer for anyone mocked or opposed for their faith leads to a result that says their friends AND family have turned against them. That is Athanasius's condition, not theirs. The teen is told his family has turned cold when his parents don't even know. The option is broad but the pairing is narrow.
findings.evidence: Greek [00365]: διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν μισούμενον καὶ διωκόμενον παρὰ πάντων τῶν τε φίλων καὶ συγγενῶν ('by all your friends and relatives'). Option text: 'People who can't stand what I believe.' Seen: 'Friends and family have turned cold because of what you believe…' Persona 3 (16, mocked by a school group, parents unaware) lands here on his first honest tap.
findings.fix: Change the option to 'My own friends and family, because of what I believe.' → P31. Add a sibling option, 'People who mock me for what I believe.' → P42 (sec 19: longing for God while enemies taunt, ἀκούσῃς τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὀνειδιζόντων). Rewrite the P42 seen line as: 'You long for God, and people keep throwing it at you: "Where is your God?"' (BSB 42:3 wording, quoted exactly).

findings.problem: The tree has no route for bereavement, one of the most common reasons anyone would take this quiz. The widow has to force a choice. Her likeliest one, 'Life. It's all just too much' → 'Making me sad', gives the seen line 'You're sad, and you can't quite say why', and that misreads her painfully: she knows exactly why.
findings.evidence: Persona 4 (widow, husband died four months ago). P42S seen: 'You're sad, and you can't quite say why.' Athanasius's section-28 remedy is general: [00545] τὸ δὲ λυποῦν θεραπεύεται, ψαλλόντων ἡμῶν ('what grieves is healed as we sing'), followed by [00546], 42:5.
findings.fix: Add a source option: 'Loss. Someone I love has died.' → P42S. Change the P42S seen line to 'Grief is weighing on you, and it won't lift.' This also fits the 'I just feel low' and 'Making me sad' routes. Change the P42S reason from 'lightens sadness' to 'Athanasius wrote that what grieves us is healed as we sing the Psalms, and the line he gave for it is this one: "Why are you downcast, O my soul?"' Do not claim he spoke about death.

findings.problem: One seen line serves two routes that contradict each other. Someone who tapped 'Life… Making me sad, and I can't shake it' knows the cause, yet is told they 'can't quite say why'.
findings.evidence: life → 'Making me sad, and I can't shake it.' → P42S. missing → 'I don't know. I just feel low.' → P42S. Seen: 'You're sad, and you can't quite say why.'
findings.fix: Use a seen line that does not assume the cause is unknown: 'Grief is weighing on you, and it won't lift.' (the same wording as the fix above).

findings.problem: Athanasius's key word here is ἀκηδιάσῃς (listless, gone numb, no heart for anything), which is the burnt-out nurse's exact state. The seen line leaves it out and says 'poor', which reads as money. And the 'Nothing's wrong, exactly. But something's missing' branch, where numb people naturally go, has no way to reach 102.
findings.evidence: Greek [00462]: διὰ τὰς συνοχὰς τοῦ βίου ὡς πτωχὸς γενόμενος ἀκηδιάσῃς ποτέ, καὶ θέλῃς παρακληθῆναι. Seen: 'Life has worn you down until you feel poor and empty, and you need comfort.' Persona 1 (a nurse, numb, praying less) who taps 'missing' ends at P42S 'You're sad', and she is numb, not sad.
findings.fix: Seen: 'Life has worn you down until you feel empty and have no heart left for anything, and you want comfort.' Add to the missing node: 'Feeling. I'm running on empty and I've gone numb.' → P102.

findings.problem: The seen line leaves out shame, which Athanasius names (ἐντραπεὶς) and which is the heart of this situation. The man whose affair has just come out would feel much more seen if it were included.
findings.evidence: Greek [00383]: Ἀλλ' ἥμαρτες, καὶ ἐντραπεὶς μεταγινώσκεις καὶ ἐλεηθῆναι ἀξιοῖς. Seen: 'You've done wrong, you know it, and you want to come back.' The reason line does keep 'ashamed'.
findings.fix: Seen: 'You've done wrong, you know it, you're ashamed, and you want to come back.'

findings.problem: The option adds a condition Athanasius never gave ('I don't know what to say') and leaves out the ones he did give: intense longing for God, and enemies taunting. It also sits under 'Nothing's wrong, exactly', which contradicts being taunted. Athanasius's advice is 'don't be troubled', not help for someone at a loss for an answer.
findings.evidence: Option: 'An answer. People ask me where God is in all this, and I don't know what to say.' Greek [00377]: πάνυ τὸν πόθον ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεόν, ἀκούσῃς τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὀνειδιζόντων, μὴ ταράσσου.
findings.fix: Remove this option from 'missing' and move P42 under 'who' as 'People who mock me for what I believe.' (see the P31 finding). If a missing-branch entry is kept, word it with both of his conditions: 'God. I long for Him, and people sneer at me for it.'

findings.problem: The option and the seen line lose the persecution that is the whole condition, so this reads as plain loneliness. It pulls in the widow and anyone lonely, then tells them they were 'pushed out'. Psalm 63:9-10 (enemies 'a portion for foxes') would then puzzle them.
findings.evidence: Greek [sec 20]: διωκόμενος εἰς ἐρημίαν ἀπέλθῃς, μὴ φοβηθῇς ὡς μόνος ὤν. Option: 'People. I've been pushed out, and I'm on my own now.' Seen: 'You've been pushed out, and you're on your own now.'
findings.fix: Option: 'People. I was driven out for what I stand for, and now I'm on my own.' Seen: 'You've been driven out for what you stand for, and you're on your own now.'

findings.problem: The option adds a temptation, 'part of me wants to agree', and so shuts out steadfast believers who are simply hearing people mock God's care, such as the teen. Athanasius's words forbid joining in; they don't say the reader wants to. Placing it under 'The wrong people keep winning' also hides it from people who are mocked for their faith.
findings.evidence: Greek [00339]: βλασφημούντων τινῶν κατὰ τῆς Προνοίας ἀκούσῃς, μὴ κοινώνει μὲν αὐτῶν τῇ ἀσεβείᾳ. Option: '…and part of me wants to agree.' Seen: '…part of you is tempted to join them.'
findings.fix: Option: 'People around me laugh at the idea that God looks after the world.' Seen: 'People around you mock the idea that God is looking after the world, and you won't join them.' Keep the reason as it is ('don't join in their contempt').

findings.problem: 'Someone I love is going through it' is ambiguous for a bereaved person. A widow reading fast may tap it and be told to 'stand beside' someone who has died.

findings.fix: Add the loss option to 'source' (the second finding above) so bereavement has its own door. Optionally reword this one to 'Someone I love is struggling, and I want to help them.'

findings.fix: Change turn from '102:12' to '102:17'.

findings.problem: For the man, the Bathsheba superscription is a direct mirror, which is powerful. But anyone who tapped 'I did something wrong' for a lesser wrong will see 'adultery' at the top of their result and may feel accused. Separately, 51:4 'Against You, You only' can read as if the wronged spouse does not count. Neither can be fixed by changing Athanasius, and the quotation must not be altered.
findings.evidence: BSB 51 superscription: 'When Nathan the prophet came to him after his adultery with Bathsheba.' 51:4 'Against You, You only, have I sinned…'
findings.fix: If superscriptions are shown, print it as the psalm's own context in small type under the psalm title, not as a headline about the reader. Add nothing that goes beyond Athanasius's advice.

findings.where: P31, P54, P57, P62, P64 (results about being hunted or threatened)
findings.problem: Children and teens will take this quiz. A bullied 16-year-old whose parents don't know gets a psalm about people plotting to take his life (31:13) and asking that they 'lie silent in Sheol' (31:17), with no pointer to a real person who can help. The owner dislikes over-explaining, so this is only a flag.
findings.evidence: BSB 31:13 'They conspire against me and plot to take my life.' 31:17 'let them lie silent in Sheol.' Persona 3.
findings.fix: On these results only, add one short line in the site's own words, outside the Athanasius paraphrase: 'If someone is hurting you, tell a person you trust.' Do not attribute it to Athanasius.

summary:
I walked the tree as the four people. Every node links to a real node or outcome, and every outcome can be reached. The problems are where options sit and how the seen lines are worded, not broken links.

1. PASTOR (false story sent to the denomination by two elders he mentored). Path: where > "In the middle of something hard" > source > "Someone is against me" > who. "Someone I trusted. A friend." leads to P55 (Psalm 55), which is the best result in the tree for him. 55:13-14 ("it is you, a man like myself, my companion... we walked with the crowd into the house of God") describes elders he walked into church with, and Athanasius's advice (praise God and be comforted) speaks to him. But the seen line ("talking about you... hurts more than you let on") undersells a false report to his denomination. If he taps "Someone with power over me" instead (just as honest: they went to the denomination), he gets P52 or P54. Psalm 52 still works for him (52:8, "an olive tree flourishing in the house of God"). Psalm 54:3 calls them "strangers", which they are not, and 54:5 says "destroy them". In both cases he never sees 55:12-14. Lines that could wound him: 55:15 ("Let death seize them"), 52:5.

2. SISTER (cut off, family turned against her). Path: hard > against me > "My own family, or the people closest to me" > P3 (Psalm 3). The seen line lands ("more and more are rising up with them"), and the superscription (David fleeing his own son) would move her if it were shown. But the reason is one bare sentence with no hope in it, "hounding" does not describe being frozen out, and 3:7 ("break the teeth of the wicked") casts a sister she still loves as "the wicked". The truest outcome for her, P63 ("pushed out, on my own"), can only be reached through "Nothing's wrong, exactly", which she would never tap.

3. STUDENT (classmates mock faith; he doubts and is scared). No source option is honest for him: the trouble is his own wavering faith. He reluctantly taps "Someone is against me" > "People who can't stand what I believe" and lands on P31 (Psalm 31). He feels misread: it says friends and FAMILY turned cold, and it assumes he is standing firm. The outcome that fits him exactly, P14 ("part of me wants to agree"), is filed under "The wrong people keep winning", which he would never pick. P42 ("Where is your God?") would also meet him, but it sits behind "Nothing's wrong, exactly" and its option asks for "an answer", not for longing. The tree has no route back when the answer to "Does this sound like you?" is no.

4. LAID-OFF MAN (money tight, feels useless, no enemy). Path: hard > "Life. It's all just too much" (reluctant: his trouble is too little, not too much) > "Wearing me down" > P102 (Psalm 102). This is a genuine hit. Athanasius's own words are "as a poor man" and "listless" (ἀκηδιάσῃς, the same words as the LXX superscription of this psalm), which name his money trouble and his uselessness. But the option text drops both, and the chosen turn line (102:12) is abstract, while 102:17 ("He will turn toward the prayer of the destitute; He will not despise their prayer") is his line. 102:10 ("You have picked me up and cast me aside") will cut him. If he taps "sad" he is told he "can't quite say why", but he can. If he taps "afraid", neither fear option is honest for him, and he lands on P91, a pairing Athanasius did not make for fear, whose "no evil will befall you" rings false to a man already struck.

Findings, most severe first, are below.

findings.problem: This pairing is stretched. Athanasius gives Psalm 91 to someone who wants to encourage themselves and others in reverence for God, showing that hope in God makes the soul unafraid. He does not give it to someone who is afraid and cannot say of what. The seen line invents the situation. The laid-off man, afraid about money, has no honest option at 'Afraid of what, mostly?', reluctantly taps 'everything', and gets 91:10 'no evil will befall you' after the disaster has already happened.
findings.evidence: [00425] Παραθαρσῦναι θέλων σεαυτὸν καὶ τοὺς ἑτέρους εἰς θεοσέβειαν, καὶ ὡς εἰς τὸν Θεὸν ἐλπὶς οὔτε καταισχύνει, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄφοβον τὴν ψυχὴν κατασκευάζει (research recon kind: 'teaching'). Draft seen: 'You're afraid, and you can't even say of what.'
findings.fix: Remove P91 from the fear node. Make the life option 'Making me afraid of what people could do to me' go straight to P118, and drop the fear node. If P91 stays, move it to the 'good' node with his situation in plain words, e.g. option 'I want to take heart in God, and help others take heart too', seen 'You want to take heart in God, and to help the people around you do the same.' Accept that fear about money has no Athanasius pairing; such a person reaches P102 through 'Wearing me down'.

findings.problem: The outcome that fits a doubter word for word is hidden under 'The way things are. The wrong people keep winning.', which a scared, doubting student would never tap. No source option names the thing he is actually living: his own faith wavering. So he is forced into 'Someone is against me' > P31 and misread.
findings.evidence: P14 option: 'People around me laugh at the idea that God is in charge, and part of me wants to agree.' Parent option: 'The way things are. The wrong people keep winning.' Greek [00339] βλασφημούντων τινῶν κατὰ τῆς Προνοίας ἀκούσῃς, μὴ κοινώνει ... ἐντυγχάνων δὲ τῷ Θεῷ.
findings.fix: Add a source option 'My faith. Part of me isn't sure any more.' leading to a new node 'faith' with two options, both real pairings: (a) 'People around me mock the idea that God is looking after anything, and part of me wants to agree.' > P14; (b) 'I want God, and people keep asking me where He is.' > P42. P14 can stay in 'world' as well.

findings.problem: The option broadens Athanasius's situation (hated by ALL friends AND relatives for the truth) to anyone who dislikes your beliefs. The mocked student lands here and is told his family turned cold and that he is holding firm, when he is wavering.
findings.evidence: Option 'People who can't stand what I believe.' vs [00365] διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν μισούμενον καὶ διωκόμενον παρὰ πάντων τῶν τε φίλων καὶ συγγενῶν. Seen: 'Friends and family have turned cold because of what you believe'.
findings.fix: Option: 'My friends and family. They've turned on me because of my faith.' Mocking classmates then go to the new 'faith' node (P14/P42).

findings.problem: Athanasius's situation is being driven into the wilderness by persecution, but it sits under 'Nothing's wrong, exactly. But something's missing.' This contradicts his situation, and the estranged sister, for whom 'pushed out and on my own' is exactly true, can never reach it: she would honestly tap 'In the middle of something hard'. The seen line also drops the fear of being alone that his advice answers.
findings.evidence: [00395] διωκόμενος εἰς ἐρημίαν ἀπέλθῃς, μὴ φοβηθῇς ὡς μόνος ὢν ἐκεῖ. Path: where > 'Nothing's wrong, exactly' > missing > 'People. I've been pushed out...'
findings.fix: Move it to node who (or source): option 'They've pushed me out. I'm on my own now.' > P63. Seen: 'You've been pushed out by people set against you, and you're afraid you're on your own now.' Remove it from 'missing'.

findings.problem: The paraphrase changes Athanasius's meaning in two ways. His gloater is ὁ διάβολος, glossed 'the devil' in research.json (the draft makes him 'the slanderer', a human), and the ruler is wicked ('wicked' is dropped from the option and the seen line). For the pastor, the devil reading is the pastoral point: it moves his anger off the elders he mentored. The option also lets any authority count, including a fair denomination.
findings.evidence: [00384] Εἰ δὲ καὶ διεβλήθης πονηρῷ βασιλεῖ, καὶ ὁρᾷς τὸν διάβολον κατακαυχώμενον, ἀναχώρει. research recon: 'seeing the devil gloat over it'. Draft reason: 'you see the slanderer boasting about it'.
findings.fix: Reason: 'If you have been slandered to a wicked ruler, and you see the devil gloating over it, step away and say Psalm 52.' Option: 'Someone lied about me to people with power over me, people who were never on my side.' If the διάβολος/διαβάλλω wordplay is judged to allow 'slanderer', say so in the sources note rather than choosing silently.

findings.problem: This is the pastor's truest result, but the wording would lose him. 'Talking about you' undersells slander (a false report to his denomination). 'Hurts more than you let on' reverses πρὸς ὀλίγον ('grieved for a little while') and adds a claim Athanasius does not make. The seen line also drops the enemies' taunts that come first in his sentence. The option 'Someone I trusted. A friend.' does not say what they did, so someone betrayed in another way would be told they are being slandered.
findings.evidence: [00391] Ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ὀνειδίζωσι θλίβοντες οἱ ἐχθροὶ, καὶ φλυαροῦντες διαβάλλωσιν οἱ δοκοῦντες εἶναι φίλοι, καὶ λυπηθῇς ἐν τῇ ἀδολεσχίᾳ σου πρὸς ὀλίγον. Seen: 'People you thought were your friends are talking about you, and it hurts more than you let on.'
findings.fix: Option: 'People I trusted. They're spreading stories about me.' Seen: 'People you thought were your friends are spreading stories about you, on top of everything else, and it has left you grieving.' Consider 55:22 ('Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you') as the hope line alongside 55:16, since 55:15 and 55:23 are imprecations a pastor will stumble on.

findings.problem: This is a genuine hit for the laid-off man, but the option text drops the two words that make it his: Athanasius's 'as a poor man' and 'listless' (ἀκηδιάσῃς, acedia, which is close to 'useless'). Both echo the LXX superscription of this psalm (Προσευχὴ τῷ πτωχῷ, ὅταν ἀκηδιάσῃ). 'Life. It's all just too much' also misdescribes a man whose trouble is too little (no work). The turn line 102:12 is cosmic, and 102:10 'You have picked me up and cast me aside' will cut someone just laid off.
findings.evidence: [00462] ἐὰν διὰ τὰς συνοχὰς τοῦ βίου ὡς πτωχὸς γενόμενος ἀκηδιάσῃς ποτὲ. Option: 'Wearing me down. I'm running on empty.' BSB 102:17 'He will turn toward the prayer of the destitute; He will not despise their prayer.'
findings.fix: Option: 'Wearing me down. I feel poor, worn out and no use to anyone.' Change turn to 102:17. Source option: 'Life. It's grinding me down.' (covers both too much and too little).

findings.problem: 'Can't quite say why' is added: Athanasius says only that the part of the soul that grieves is healed by singing 42:5. It fits the 'missing > I just feel low' route but misreads anyone arriving through life > 'Making me sad', such as the laid-off man, who knows exactly why.
findings.evidence: [00545] τὸ δὲ λυποῦν θεραπεύεται, ψαλλόντων ἡμῶν· [00546] Ἵνα τί περίλυπος εἶ, ἡ ψυχή μου. Seen: 'You're sad, and you can't quite say why.'
findings.fix: Seen: 'Something is weighing your soul down, and you can't shake it.' (true for both routes).

findings.problem: For the estranged sister the seen line lands, but the result gives her almost nothing: a one-sentence reason with no hope in it. 'Hounding' does not describe being frozen out, and 3:7 ('break the teeth of the wicked') casts a sister she still loves as 'the wicked', with nothing to frame it. Athanasius said more about Psalm 3 in §12, and the psalm's own superscription is the strongest thing it has for her.
findings.evidence: [00326] Ἂν δὲ διώκῃ παρὰ τῶν ἰδίων ... λέγε τὸν γʹ ψαλμόν. [00221] Ὅτε γοῦν τὸν τρίτον ψάλλει τις εἰς τὰς ἰδίας θλίψεις συνορῶν, ὡς αὑτοῦ εἶναι νομίζει τὰ ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ ῥήματα. BSB superscription: 'when he fled from his son Absalom'.
findings.fix: Reason: 'When your own people turn on you, and many rise up with them, say Psalm 3. David prayed it running from his own son. Athanasius adds that when you pray it with your own trouble in mind, you will find its words are yours (§§12, 15).' Keep turn 3:3; consider also showing 3:5 ('I lie down and sleep; I wake again, for the LORD sustains me').

findings.where: general (the 'Does this sound like you?' step)
findings.problem: The tree does not say what happens if someone answers No. The student at P31 is misread and has nowhere to go, so the quiz dead-ends at exactly the moment it fails to see him.
findings.evidence: Every outcome has 'seen' shown as 'Does this sound like you?', but no field or node handles a No.
findings.fix: Define the No path in the data: return to the last question with the tapped option greyed out (or show the sibling outcomes' seen lines as 'Is it more like this?').

findings.problem: The option asks for an intellectual answer; Athanasius's situation is intense longing for God while enemies taunt you. So the option and the seen line describe different people. Tucked under 'Nothing's wrong, exactly', it is also out of reach for the scared student it best fits.
findings.evidence: Option: 'An answer. People ask me where God is in all this, and I don't know what to say.' vs [00377] πάνυ τὸν πόθον ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεὸν, ἀκούσῃς τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὀνειδιζόντων. Seen: 'You long for God, and people keep asking you where He is.'
findings.fix: Option: 'I want God, and people keep asking me where He is.' Place it in the new 'faith' node (see the P14 finding) as well as, or instead of, 'missing'.

For someone estranged from family, the draft's reading could push them toward cutting family off, which Athanasius does not clearly say.

findings.problem: The option drops 'against God's people', so the pastor (the denomination is 'far bigger than I am') could tap it and get a Goliath psalm about a tyrant attacking God's people. That is a stretch of the pairing.
findings.evidence: [§25] a tyrant enemy rising against God's people and against you, as Goliath did (research recon entry 86). Option: 'They're coming after me, and they're far bigger than I am.'

findings.evidence: [00329] Αἰσθόμενος δὲ ἀπειλῆς τοῦ Κυρίου, ἐὰν διὰ τοῦτο ταραττόμενον σεαυτὸν βλέπῃς. Seen: 'It feels as if God is against you right now, and it's shaking you.'
findings.fix: Seen: 'You sense God warning you, and it's shaking you.'

findings.problem: Of the choices open to someone under long attack, only P62 fits 'I'm holding on and waiting'. There is an honest, unused pairing for the person enduring under attack who wants to know what patience gains, which suits the pastor and the sister.
findings.evidence: research recon entry 38, §19: [00375] τῶν ἐχθρῶν ἐπιτιθεμένων, ὑπομένῃς τὰς θλίψεις, καὶ θέλῃς μαθεῖν τὴν ἐκ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ὠφέλειαν, ψάλλε τὸν λθʹ (Eng 40).
findings.fix: Add to 'pull': 'To keep waiting it out, and I need to know it's worth it.' > new outcome P40 (Psalm 40), seen: 'You're holding on under attack, and you want to know that the waiting is worth something.'

summary:
I walked all four people through the quiz, starting at "start". Two of them are served well: the envious man and, mostly, the new believer. The other two get a result that is either invented or harmful.

PERSONA 1, the woman who is anxious for no reason and lies awake. None of the four first answers fits her. "In the middle of something hard" assumes something happened. "Nothing's wrong, exactly. But something's missing" gets half of it right, but nothing is missing for her. She most likely taps where > "In the middle of something hard" > "Life. It's all just too much" (she chooses it reluctantly, because "source" has no "I can't tell where it's coming from") > "Making me afraid" > "Of everything, and nothing in particular" > P91.
- The "seen" line would make her feel very seen ("You're afraid, and you can't even say of what"). Psalm 91:5 ("You will not fear the terror of the night") lands for someone awake at night.
- But Athanasius never named this situation. The Greek (§22, line 00425) is a teaching aim: "Wanting to encourage yourself and others toward godliness, [showing] that hope in God does not shame but makes the soul fearless." The "reason" line therefore does not answer the "seen" line. It tells a frightened woman to encourage others in reverence. This breaks the real-data rule.
- Her other likely path is where > missing > "I don't know. I just feel low." > P42S. That line says "You're sad", and she is not sad; she is uneasy. Yet the verse Athanasius quotes for sadness in §28 is 42:5, which the BSB gives as "Why the unease within me?" (the Greek has "why do you trouble me"). §28 also gives 118:6 for fear in general. So the honest results for her already exist in the draft; the tree just does not lead her to them.

PERSONA 2, the new believer baptised a month ago. where > "In a good place" > "I just want to thank Him for everything" > P103.
- "You want to thank God, in and through everything" fits her, though it says nothing about her being new.
- Psalm 103 meets her strongly: 103:3 "forgives all your iniquities" and 103:12 "as far as the east is from the west". Athanasius's advice ("stir up your own soul") suits her.
- Her other plausible tap is "I'm growing. I'm leaving old things behind" > P120. That result shows Psalm 120 as her psalm: "Deliver my soul... from lying lips", "Woe to me that I dwell in Meshech", "when I speak, they want war". That is a jarring answer to joy, and the "names" line points at 121:1, a different psalm.
- Nothing in "good" names a new beginning, although Athanasius made honest pairings for it: Ps 32 (§18), Ps 15 (§16) and the praise set (§24).

PERSONA 3, the mother whose son is seriously ill. where > middle > "Someone I love is going through it." > "Someone I love is suffering, and I want to be there for them." > P20.
- The "seen" line only half reads her: "you want to stand beside them" leaves out her fear and her constant praying.
- Psalm 20 is a prayer she can say over her son ("May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble"). Athanasius's advice (comfort them, pray over them, say these words to them) gives her something to do, which helps.
- Some lines could hurt her if he does not recover. 20:4-5 ("make all your plans succeed... shout for joy at your victory") and 20:6 ("the LORD saves His anointed") read like a promised outcome. The king-and-chariots imagery feels far from a sickbed. P20 has no "turn" line.
- The "loved" node has no "I'm scared for them and all I can do is pray" answer. Athanasius gives Ps 5 and 143 for "wanting to pray and plead" (§25), and 118:6 for fear (§28).
- If she answers through the fear branch instead, she reaches P91: "nor the pestilence that stalks in the darkness" (91:6) and "no plague will approach your tent" (91:10). For a mother of a very sick child, that is a wound.

PERSONA 4, the honest man whose rival cheated his way to success. where > middle > "The way things are. The wrong people keep winning." > "People who cheat and lie are doing fine, and good people are struggling." > P73. This is the best result in the walk.
- The pairing matches §21 exactly.

summary:
Overall the draft passes the owner's test far better than the scrapped batch. Most screens sound like a wise friend talking, and each tap follows from the last one ("Who are they to you?", "What is it doing to you?"). Most "seen" lines are specific and human, and some are excellent: "it hurts more than you let on" (P55), "part of me wants to agree" (P14) and the "children's arrows" line (P64).

The problems fall into five groups:
1. **A mistranslation.** P137 renders ἀλλοτρίων λογισμῶν as "someone else's way of thinking". The Greek means stray, sinful thoughts: in line [00475] he goes on to "where you caught yourself sinning".
2. **Options that look alike on a phone.** "Trying to ruin me, and they won't let up" and "It just won't end" sit on the same screen. So do P4 and P46, which are both "I called and God helped". On the Who screen, family (P3), friend (P55) and "people who can't stand what I believe" (P31) overlap, and P31's option points at outsiders while its "seen" line says friends and family.
3. **One loaded option.** "To stay calm and trust God, even though it's hard" is the obvious right answer, and it is the only option on that screen that mentions God.
4. **Wrong placement and entry labels.** P63 (driven out by persecution) sits under "Nothing's wrong, exactly". The labels on the "source" screen promise less than their branches hold: "wrong people keep winning" does not cover P12 or P14, and "Someone I love" does not cover P41.
5. **Additions and clichés.** Some options add a cause or a virtue Athanasius never gave: "Everything keeps going wrong" (P6), "refusing to go along" (P34), "without giving in" (P139). There are also a few clichés and vague words: "storm", "growing", "poor", the ownerless "the anger", and "Which is closest/closer?" used three times.

Two screens are too long for a phone ("doing" has 6 options, "out" has 7). Two reasons (P42S, P118) switch to a third-person "Athanasius wrote" voice. P42S also softens his verb: "healed" (θεραπεύεται) becomes "lightens".

Pronoun capitals are correct throughout, the BSB quotation at 42:5 matches, and I found no preachy or jargon-heavy lines except "not yet anointed" (P27) and a clunky parenthesis in P39. Each finding gives exact replacement wording.

summary:
Reverent capitals are clean. I checked every option, "seen" and "reason" string, and every pronoun for God is capitalised. The one lowercase "his" (P144, "sing his words") refers to David, which is correct.

The real problems are pastoral. The draft sends its most vulnerable paths straight into lines that could hurt or mislead:
- **Next blow (P64):** "waiting for the next blow" leads to "their blows will be like children's arrows". That line is Septuagint wording and does not appear in the BSB text the page prints.
- **Verdict (P26):** "don't hand the verdict to any human being" can be read as "don't report it".
- **Submit (P62):** "the more they rage, the more you yield" can be heard as advice to submit to the person hurting you.
- **Two new ideas added:** P6 tells people whose lives are going wrong that God is correcting them, and P91 turns a teaching entry into an answer for free-floating fear.

Three situations change Athanasius's meaning:
- **P137:** "captive to alien thoughts, repenting where you caught yourself sinning" became "carried off by other people's thinking". This also drops the repentance, which is his point.
- **P85:** God's anger ending became "the storm is over".
- **P34:** turning aside from their plot became "refusing to go along with something".

The imprecations need one fixed pattern:
- Print every psalm whole and unaltered. Athanasius himself forbids reworking the words (TLG [00567], §31).
- Add one quiet note at the first hard line, grounded in his §17 counsel to ask God to judge (TLG [00354]-[00355]).
- Never let a result end on a curse or a bleak last line.
- For Psalm 137, cite Augustine's reading of 137:9 (little ones = sinful desires dashed on the Rock, Who is Christ), credited to Augustine and not to Athanasius. It fits Athanasius's own framing, captivity to thoughts, exactly.

Nothing in the draft needs cutting outright. Keep 58, 59, 83 and 109 out, as the draft already does.

For people in crisis:
- Show one fixed two-line safety note on hard-branch results.
- Add an "It's worse than that" answer at the "Does this sound like you?" step. It leads to help first, then Athanasius's own words for extremity (57 and 142).
- Add one line on the dangerous paths: David fled (the psalms' own superscriptions say so), and Paul appealed to Caesar.

Traditions: show the Greek numbering once so Orthodox and older Catholic readers can follow. Never claim completeness, since Psalm 151 and most of the letter's pairings are not used.

Show the "also" psalms as links with a single line each, never printed in full. Fix 116 to 116:1-9.
